name: Jumping pose
blurb: Mid-air, feet off the ground: the most energetic pose for drawings and photos
title: Jumping Pose Reference: Mid-Air Poses for Drawing & Photography
description: Jumping pose reference for artists and photographers: star jumps, tucked and leg-kick poses, drawing mid-air motion and shutter settings that freeze a jump.
answer: A jumping pose shows the figure in the air with both feet off the ground. The clearest jumps freeze one moment, usually the peak where the body hangs still for a split second, and exaggerate the limbs into a strong shape such as a star, a tuck or a leg kick.

sections.h: What a jump pose is for
body: Jumps signal joy, celebration and energy. They are popular for graduation and travel photos, group shots and character art for cheerful or sporty characters. Because the feet leave the ground, hair, skirts and sleeves lift and trail, which adds a lot of motion with very little effort.
A jump has three readable phases: take-off with the body extended, the peak with limbs spread or tucked, and landing with the knees bending. Most reference photos and illustrations use the peak.

sections.h: How to draw a jumping figure
body: Start with a long, curved line of action; a jump should never be drawn on a straight vertical. Leave visible space under the feet and add a small shadow on the ground away from the figure to prove it is airborne.

Push the shape further than feels comfortable: arms higher, knees tighter, back more arched. Secondary elements follow the motion with a delay, so on the way up hair and cloth hang down, and at the peak they float. Avoid placing both feet at the same height and angle; asymmetry keeps the pose alive.

Freeze the motion with a shutter speed of about 1/1000 s or faster in daylight, and use burst mode, since the peak lasts only a fraction of a second. Pre-focus on the spot where the subject will jump.

ul: Shoot from low down, around knee height, so the jump looks higher against the sky.
Leave headroom in the frame; the subject will rise more than you expect.
Count down out loud so everyone in a group jumps together.
Choose shoes with grip and a flat surface; skip jumps in long or tight costumes.

faq.q: What shutter speed do I need for jumping photos?
faq.a: Around 1/1000 s or faster freezes most jumps sharply. Use burst mode to catch the peak.

faq.q: How do I make a jump look higher in photos?
faq.a: Shoot from a low angle, keep the horizon low in the frame and ask the subject to tuck the knees at the peak.

faq.q: How do I show that a drawn character is in the air?
faq.a: Leave space under the feet, cast a separate shadow on the ground, and let hair and clothing float or trail.
